title: The Sales-to-Customer-Success Handoff Template: Goals, Promises, and Open Questions
summary: A sales-to-customer-success handoff should transfer the customer's intended outcome, the promises made, and the decisions still open.
body_markdown:
A sales-to-customer-success handoff should transfer the customer’s intended outcome, the promises made, and the decisions still open. The receiving team needs enough context to continue the relationship without asking the customer to repeat the sale.


Treat the handoff as an accepted transfer of responsibility. Uploading notes or tagging a colleague is not sufficient when nobody has confirmed that the information is usable and the next action is owned.


## Copy the handoff template


Section Questions to answer


Customer objective Why did the customer buy? What outcome matters first?


Scope What is included, excluded, and still unconfirmed?


Stakeholders Who sponsors the work, uses the product, and approves decisions?


Commitments What was promised, by whom, and with what timing?


Evidence Where are the relevant agreement, messages, and decisions?


Dependencies What must the customer or our team provide before work can proceed?


Open questions What still requires clarification or a specialist?


Risks What could disrupt the plan, and what evidence supports that concern?


Next action What happens next, who owns it, and when will the customer hear from us?


Acceptance Who reviewed the packet and accepted responsibility?


Use plain language. The document should help someone act, not demonstrate how much information the seller collected. Link to detail when the full record is needed.


## Capture the reason behind the purchase


“Bought the enterprise plan” describes a transaction. It does not explain the customer’s goal. Write the problem they intend to solve and the first outcome they expect. Preserve the customer’s wording where it is useful and authorised to share internally.


Identify the difference between a sponsor’s goal and a user’s immediate task. A sponsor may want a more consistent process, while users need to complete one workflow without friction. Both matter to onboarding, but they require different evidence of progress.


If the goal is unclear, do not invent one. Ask the seller to identify the relevant discovery evidence or arrange a focused clarification. The question should build on what the customer has already said rather than restart discovery.


## Separate promises from possibilities


Commercial conversations contain requests, estimates, aspirations, and commitments. Label them accurately. “We will confirm whether this is supported” does not mean “this is supported.” A target date should not become a guaranteed delivery date when copied into a handoff.


For each commitment, record its source, owner, and timing. If a seller made a promise that requires another team’s work, confirm that team’s acceptance. If the promise cannot be fulfilled as stated, resolve the discrepancy promptly and communicate responsibly.


See[customer commitment tracking](https://o11.ai/blog/customer-commitment-tracking) for a practical register. The handoff should create continuity, not a hidden backlog of obligations nobody agreed to own.


## Worked example


This example is illustrative. A customer wants its operations team to complete a first workflow before inviting a second group. The seller has promised setup instructions before Friday and a discussion about the second group’s requirements.


The handoff records the initial workflow as the first-value milestone. It names the customer’s administrator as the access dependency. It links to the request for instructions and notes that the second group’s scope remains unconfirmed.


The next action is for the onboarding owner to review the setup requirements, confirm the instruction delivery, and propose a kickoff. The commercial opportunity is not labelled “ready to expand.” It remains a customer need to investigate after the initial team can proceed.


This packet prevents two mistakes: forgetting the near-term promise and treating an exploratory question as a settled commercial decision.


## Define acceptance criteria


The receiving owner should verify that the customer identity is correct, the objective is understandable, and the next action is achievable. They should be able to locate the important source documents and identify unresolved questions.


If the packet is incomplete, return a specific request rather than rejecting the entire account indefinitely. For example: “Please confirm who can approve access; the other information is sufficient to begin preparation.” Assign an owner and review point to the missing item.


Create a backup acceptance route when the normal owner is absent. The customer should not wait because an internal assignment rule sent the handoff to someone on leave.


## Introduce the new owner thoughtfully


A useful introduction explains the role of the receiving person and the next step. It should also demonstrate continuity: “Maya will help your operations team reach the first workflow milestone we discussed. She has the setup questions and the Friday instruction commitment.”


Do not expose sensitive internal notes or speculative risk labels in the introduction. Prepare a customer-safe version that reflects confirmed facts. Check names, roles, dates, and scope before sending.


The[onboarding email templates](https://o11.ai/blog/customer-onboarding-email-templates) provide examples for the first messages after transfer.


## Measure handoff quality


Track missing information, customer repetition, unaccepted handoffs, and commitments discovered late. These are closer to the handoff’s purpose than the number of documents created.


Review failures with both teams. If a field is consistently missing, determine whether it is difficult to collect, unclear, or unnecessary. Keep the packet small enough to maintain and precise enough to support the receiving owner.


[HubSpot’s handoff playbook](https://cdn2.hubspot.net/hubfs/137828/_Academy%20Education%20-%20Learning%20Center%20Resources/Academy_Sales%20to%20CS%20handoff/Sales%20to%20CS%20handoff%20playbook%20%281%29%20copy.pdf) is an additional process reference. To evaluate o11,[bring an approved handoff example](https://o11.ai/demo) and ask it to preserve the goals, source-backed promises, and open questions without inventing certainty.
